patterns.what_worked: One per-family id table (steady_id_by_family) behind BOTH the guide slot and the HUD slot, so the two surfaces cannot disagree; the HUD re-point mirrors the Aimed Shot mirror that already existed; the strict HU-13 sweep immediately exposed 46 rotation rows that declared no engine flag at all - the truthiness test had been certifying them as engine-facing since the utility lane landed.
patterns.what_was_hard: The Era client: the shipped tree drops the Steady SLOT on Era while the gather's range probe reads 56641 there - the two statements contradict each other and the corpus only makes a bench claim (no client read). Resolved by keeping the Era behaviour byte-identical (the probe still reads 56641) and filing the question with the observation that settles it (GetSpellInfo(56641) on 1.15.9). The CATA/MISTS/RETAIL Steady id (49052) has no client citation - marked CLIENT-UNCONFIRMED in the code comment, and the runtime resolution replaces it with the client's own rank.
patterns.skill_gap: The Era Steady Shot question could not be settled from the corpus alone; a corpus-vs-tree contradiction needs a client read, not another bench claim. Also: the hunter was the only class whose rotation rows omitted the engine flag, which the truthiness pins hid - the other five classes already declared both flags, so the house convention was there to copy.
